question.text: The potential energy of a particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> in motion along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">U</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The time period of the particle for small oscillation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>≃</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Given here, potential energy, U=41-cos4x J

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy, F=-dUdx.

We have, F=-4+sin4x4=-16sin4x

For small θ, sinθ≈θ.

Acceleration of particle is a=-64xm=-64x4=-16x

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so  a=-ω2x⇒ω2=16⇒ω=4 rad s-1

Now, time period of oscillation isT=2πω=π2.

Thus, the value of K=2.
